_why: MP-603. Every CI step that can reach the production Supabase project (xrzweoneiieddzxogewk) is listed here, classified read or write, by a human who read it. check-prod-write-ref-gate.mjs refuses to grade an unclassified population: a NEW prod-touching step is RED even when the guard does not recognise the verb it uses, which is the failure a vocabulary-only matcher cannot avoid (MP-399: a dead status='error' filter matched no rows and printed green for its entire life).
_rules: classification=write AND the workflow admits a non-main ref => the step must AND in a ref gate. Keys are file::job::step and are matched exactly; a stale key is RED so a deleted write's slot cannot be silently reused (MP-356: count-only floors are fungible). MP-606: a classification outside ["read","write"] is RED (one transposed letter used to demote a real write to ungraded), and a "read" claim is RED when the guard's own evidence refutes it -- a write command in command position, or a SQL payload whose statement mutates. That CONTRADICTS a read claim; it cannot PROVE one. `Fire critical jobs` below is a write whose payload is `SELECT <fn>::text`, and no matcher can see a side effect behind a SELECT, so the human `why` is still load-bearing. Proof: npm run prove:prod-write-census-claims.

deploy-supabase.yml::deploy::Sync rotate.why: runs `supabase secrets set` against prod. Fired successfully twice from an unmerged branch (runs 33531886227 / 33548643802, pull_request, codex/apex-imo-vsl-rewrite-20260901) before MP-602 gated it.

deploy-supabase.yml::deploy::Deploy edge.why: runs `supabase functions deploy`. This is the step that deployed to prod from 35 non-main refs over 758 runs (MP-602).

deploy-supabase.yml::deploy::Apply migra.why: runs `supabase db push`. 0 migrations ever applied from a non-main ref, but only because migrations are hand-applied via bot-sql before CI sees them - an accident of workflow, not a safety property.

external-cron-backup.yml::heartbeat::Fir.why: POSTs `SELECT <fn>()` to bot-sql and calls edge functions to fire pg_cron jobs that dropped. Executing those functions is the point of the workflow; they have side effects in prod.

vantage-production-sync.yml::sync::Fetch.why: scripts/sync-vantage-production.ts runs `insert into public.production_external_daily_snapshots ... on conflict do update` via bot-sql. The workflow YAML names the prod ref zero times, so a YAML-only scan cannot see this.

deploy-supabase.yml::deploy::Deploy cred.why: capability probe. Echoes the sentence 'supabase secrets set was skipped' in a message, which is why the matcher requires command position.

deploy-supabase.yml::deploy::Prod writes.why: echo-only. Writes the job summary explaining why prod writes were withheld.

deploy-supabase.yml::deploy::Summary.why: echo-only into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Reaches the census solely because it prints $PROJECT_REF.

deploy-supabase.yml::deployed-source-aud.why: audit. No write verb anywhere in scripts/check-deployed-function-source.mjs.
audit. Its only `supabase functions deploy` occurrence is inside a remediation message it prints on failure.

external-cron-backup.yml::heartbeat::Che.why: SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ...) against cron.job_run_details. Reaches prod only through the job-level $BOT_SQL env var - it names nothing itself, which is how the first cut of the guard missed it.
